- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or shows strong downward momentum, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion or panic-driven volatility.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots in subsequent periods; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., 1–2 consecutive days of 0.00 or 1.00), model exhibits lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion in 10–15 day windows; apply a 10–15 day smoothing filter or use sentiment-weighted moving average for mid-term correction.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00–0.33) or volatile, model tends to overfit recent noise; reduce forecast volatility by 15–20% to avoid overreaction to short-term sentiment swings.
